html:
By a law of 19 March 1946, Martinique, Guadeloupe, French Guiana and Reunion stopped being colonies and became overseas departments of France, with the same status as departments at home.

The law was written by Aime Cesaire and other deputies from the colonies, who hoped it would bring equal rights, wages and welfare. It came as other colonies were moving toward independence.

Departmentalisation brought French schools, health care and social benefits, and much higher incomes than on nearby independent islands. But prices stayed high, jobs were few, and many young people left for France. Strikes in 2009 against the cost of living showed the tensions. Most voters have chosen to stay French, unlike the islands of the old British Empire.
sum: By a law of 19 March 1946, Martinique, Guadeloupe, French Guiana and Reunion stopped being colonies and became overseas departments of France, with the same status as departments at home.
